# CharacterBody

- Inherits [`BasePart`](basepart.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("CharacterBody")`

A capsule that walks: a player's character, or anything that should climb a ramp and step over a curb instead of tumbling. It is a character controller, not a rigid body. It moves at the velocity your script gives it through `Move` and never tips over.

The whole character is this one instance.

Two characters block each other, and neither pushes the other. Walking into a character that is standing still stops you and leaves it in place. To shove or knock back another character, move it from a script. Whether two characters collide is decided by `CollisionGroup`, as for any two parts.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AutoStepHeight` | `number` | `0.5` | read/write | The height of the tallest ledge the character steps over instead of being stopped by, in meters. At 0, a curb stops it. |
| `FloorMaterial` | `Material?` | — | read-only | The material the character is standing on: the material of the part under it, or the terrain layer drawn under its feet. It is what `RaycastResult.Material` reports for a ray cast straight down.<br><br>It is nil in the air, in water and on a part with no material. Read its `FootstepSound` for a footstep, and its `Friction` or `Tags` to treat ice or mud differently. |
| `FlySpeed` | `number` | `16` | read/write | The speed at which `Move` moves the character while `Flying` is on, in meters per second. |
| `Flying` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the character flies: gravity does not affect it, and `Move` uses all three axes at `FlySpeed`. Use it for a creative mode, a ghost or a jetpack. |
| `GravityScale` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much of `Workspace.Gravity` affects the character. 1 is all of it, 0.5 gives a floaty jump, and 0 is none. With a negative value the character falls upward. |
| `Grounded` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether the character was standing on walkable ground at the last simulation tick. It is true exactly when `State` is `Grounded`. |
| `JumpSpeed` | `number` | `8` | read/write | The upward speed that `Jump` gives the character, in meters per second. The height of the jump depends on `Workspace.Gravity`. A negative value launches the character downward. |
| `MaxSlopeAngle` | `number` | `46` | read/write | The steepest ground the character can stand and walk on, in degrees from horizontal. On steeper ground it slides down. |
| `State` | `Enum.CharacterState` | — | read-only | What the character is doing.<br><br>- `Grounded`: standing on walkable ground. - `Airborne`: not supported. Ground too steep to walk on also reads as `Airborne`. - `Swimming`: its middle is below the surface of a `Water` or inside a fluid block. The character enters and leaves this state by itself. - `Flying`: `Flying` is on. |
| `SwimSpeed` | `number` | `10` | read/write | The speed at which `Move` moves the character through a fluid, in meters per second. |
| `WalkSpeed` | `number` | `16` | read/write | The speed at which `Move` moves the character along the ground, in meters per second. The direction given to `Move` is multiplied by this, so a direction of length 0.5 walks at half speed. |

## Methods

### `Jump()`

Launches the character upward at `JumpSpeed` at the next simulation tick.

It does not check whether the character is on the ground, so that a double jump or a wall jump can be written with the same call. For an ordinary jump, check first: `if character.Grounded then character:Jump() end`. Calling it every frame makes the character fly.

### `Move(direction: vector)`

Sets the direction the character moves in during the next simulation tick, in world space. Call it every tick while the character should move; a character that is not told to move stops.

On foot, only the horizontal part of the direction is used; gravity and `Jump` control the vertical motion. The direction is multiplied by `WalkSpeed` and is not normalized, so a shorter vector walks more slowly. While swimming or flying, all three axes are used, at `SwimSpeed` or `FlySpeed`.

A character can be pushed like a part. `ApplyImpulse` changes its velocity by the impulse divided by its `Mass`, and `LinearVelocity` can be set, for a knockback or a launch pad. The push fades, quickly on the ground and slowly in the air, and the walk is added to it.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Landed(groundPart: BasePart?)`

Fires when the character becomes `Grounded` after being `Airborne`. Passes the part it landed on, or nil when it landed on terrain.
